REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Georgia

Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor - Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project TCTC-GATE

Loan No. 9981-GE

Project No. P513957

Assignment Title: Chief Advisor on Road Infrastructure Engineering

Reference No: TCTC-GATE/CS/ICS-02

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank towards the cost of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor - Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (TCTC-GATE) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, and related services and consulting services to be procured under this project, which will be jointly financed by the Government of Georgia.

Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the following services: Chief Advisor on Road Infrastructure Engineering. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The CVs of the candidates should cover the requested information. Interested individuals shall provide CV demonstrating that they have the necessary experience to perform the aforesaid services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/gvguksn6p9e42nvybjj58/TOR_International_Road_Advisor_as-submitted-in-STEP-22.09.2026.pdf?rlkey=jj5ojzz9o8vmyhx7s8hx0a95l&dl=0

Required Qualification of the Consultant:

  • Master’s Degree or equivalent in Civil Engineering/Highway Engineering/bridges and structural engineering/Geotechnical Engineering; A PhD degree will be considered an advantage
  • At least 20 years of professional experience in the management and implementation of large-scale road infrastructure projects;
  • including  10 years of international professional experience in providing engineering and contractual advisory services;
  • Proven experience in assessment of project options and recommendation of sector-specific decisions and support for projects implementation with public sector institutions;
  • Experience working in complex geological conditions, high-mountain environments, and seismically active regions is desired;
  • Experience in developing and/or managing climate-resilient infrastructure projects is desired.
  • Preference will be given to candidates with experience in road surface condition assessments and the development of road pavement design, maintenance, rehabilitation, and upgrade solutions.
  • Experience working under the latest editions of FIDIC Red Book and/or Yellow Book contracts;
  • Experience working on projects financed by development partners (including ADB, WB, EIB, AIIB, EBRD and others);
  • Experience in the implementation of projects in landslide-prone and rockfall-prone areas;
  • Excellent command of the English language.

Note: The Road Department reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The period of the consultancy services shall be 24 months (with possibility of the extension, subject to satisfactory performance) and the remuneration will be time-based.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the Client under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address: info@georoad.ge.

Expressions of Interest accompanied by CVs and other relevant information electronically or in printed materials must be delivered to the address below not later than October 30, 2026, 18:00 hours.

  4. The consultant shall be contracted for an initial period of twenty-four (24) calendar months from the contract commencement date. This period is subject to extension up to the project closing date, based on project needs, availability of funds, and satisfactory performance.
  5. The State Department for Agriculture (the “Client”) through the Food Systems Resilience Project now invites eligible individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested individuals MUST provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, professional qualifications.

The shortlisting criteria are as follows;

i)  KE-MOALF- 569688-CS-INDV-Data Science expert 1 and KE-MOALF-570715-CS- INDV- Data Science expert 2

  1. A minimum of a Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, or another relevant quantitative field from a recognized institution.
  2. At least five (5) years of demonstrable general professional experience in managing and analysing large institutional datasets, developing statistical models, and applying statistical analysis and data-mining techniques.
  3. At least three (3) years of demonstrable specific professional experience in the use of statistical and data-mining tools and techniques, database querying and management, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), distributed data-processing systems, and High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments.

ii.  KE-MOALF-571589-CS-INDV; System Analyst

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Business Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in systems analysis, business-process analysis or information systems implementation.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in requirements engineering, business-process modelling, functional specifications, systems integration analysis, system testing, user acceptance testing and requirements traceability.

    iii. KE-MOALF-571591-CS-INDV; Learning Designer Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Communication, Instructional Design, Learning Design, Educational Technology, E-Learning, Curriculum Development, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in learning design, instructional design, curriculum/content development or digital learning.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in digital learning design, instructional content development, storyboarding, assessment design, learner engagement, e-learning development and learning evaluation.

      iv. KE-MOALF-571593-CS-INDV; Webmaster Expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Web Development, Digital Media, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in website administration and web operations.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in CMS administration, website maintenance, web security, backups and restoration, performance optimization, web analytics, accessibility and content publishing.

    v. KE-MOALF-571594-CS-INDV; User Interface Developer       

  1.  A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in user interface/front-end development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in responsive web/mobile interfaces, reusable components, API integration, accessibility, usability, cross-browser/device testing and interface performance optimization.

vi. KE-MOALF-571595-CS-INDV; Backend developer expert

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in backend/software development.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in server-side application development, RESTful APIs, systems integration, secure coding, database-backed services, automated testing, performance optimization and production deployments.

     vii. KE-MOALF-571596-CS-INDV; Database Administrator

  1. A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Database Administration, Software Engineering, or a related field from a university/institution recognized in Kenya.
  2. At least five (5) years’ demonstrable general experience in database administration and management.
  3. At least three (3) years’ demonstrable specific experience in enterprise database administration, database performance tuning, backup and recovery, database security and access management, high availability, database monitoring and database lifecycle management.                           6. Assignment Title: International Road/Highway Engineer

Reference No. KCIP/CS/ICS-03R

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kakheti Connectivity Improvement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the following services: International Road/Highway Engineer. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The CVs of the candidates should cover the requested information.

International Road/Highway Engineer will assist the Roads Department in ensuring full compliance with Georgian laws, relevant technical regulations, engineering standards, World Bank requirements, and internationally recognized practices. This role involves close daily collaboration with RD and encompasses tasks such as preparing road designs, supervising construction activities, coordinating site visits, and other related duties.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/bn63drcck68imzznjppj8/TOR_Road-Highway-Engineer.pdf?rlkey=f6dqekhsxc8abpjk4r2pj9j3w&dl=0

The Qualification Requirements for selection of the Consultant are as follows:

  • Master`s Degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering, or a related field with 8 years of experience in road projects on a similar position;
  • Minimum of 5 years of International experience in road design/construction/reconstruction/rehabilitation and/or construction supervision assignments on a similar position;
  • Proven experience in preparing detailed design and/or Design Review assignments for highways and related infrastructure;
  • Solid knowledge of geometric design standards, pavement design, hydrological and drainage solutions, and structural requirements for artificial structures (bridges, culverts, retaining walls, etc.);
  • Experience in coordinating multidisciplinary teams (geologists, hydrologists, environmental specialists, cost estimators, etc.) and ensuring integration of their outputs into road projects;
  • Experience of working in institutional and physical environments similar to those prevailing;
  • Ability to utilize and share knowledge and best international practices to benefit works contractors and supervisions consultants;
  • Ability to work both independently and within teams;
  • Possess superior verbal and writing communication skills in English language.

 

The period of the consultancy services shall be 24 months (with possibility of downstream extension, subject to satisfactory performance) and the remuneration will be time-based.

Note: The Road Department reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh, Edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the Client under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants set out in the Procurement Regulations.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)
(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

TÜRKYE

Climate and Disaster Resilient Cities Project
Credit No: 9443-TR

Assignment Title: Implementation Support Consultant for the Climate and Disaster Resilient Cities Project: Consultancy Services to Provide Technical and Legal Support to Property Owners for Resilient Housing Reconstruction/Retrofitting and Verification/Inspections of Retrofitting/Reconstruction Activities in zmir

Reference No.: TCDRCP-C1-CS-TECHLEGAL-01.01

  1. The Urban Transformation Presidency (UTP) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Climate and Disaster Resilient Cities Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.
  2. The Consultant shall perform the assignment in accordance with the contract and its annexes and shall provide consulting services for approximately 24 months or latest until October 31, 2028, from the contract start date. All buildings shall remain under the liability of the consulting firm throughout the duration of the consulting contract and until the occupancy certificate of the buildings is obtained.
    Additionally, the general goal and intent of the consulting services ("Provision of Technical and Legal Support") are:

• To provide technical and legal support to property owners of at-risk residential and/or commercial units regarding the contracts to be signed between the property owners and contractors for the strengthening/reconstruction of such units under Component 2 of the Project.
• To conduct technical verification, supervision, monitoring, and reporting during and after the construction phase of the works carried out by contractors in close cooperation with the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization, and Climate Change (MoEUCC) and building inspection firms, particularly in terms of quality, durability, feasibility, time, and cost, for the buildings selected through a sampling methodology by the UTP PMU.
• To fulfill all audits and tasks requested by the UTP PMU during project implementation.
• To support the UTP PMU in handling complaints.

  1. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the services are attached to this invitation. 
  2. The detailed Terms of References (TORs) for the assignments can be found at the following web page address: https://kentseldirenclilik.csb.gov.tr/
  3. The Directorate of Urban Transformation invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.
  4. A consulting firm may submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) individually if it believes it is fully capable of carrying out the assignment alone. It is not mandatory for consultants, whether foreign or local, to form a partnership with any other firm(s). Alternatively, if consultants prefer to enhance their qualifications and capacity for the assignment, such partnerships may be formed as a Joint Venture (where all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or as Sub-consultants (where the Consultant shall be responsible for the services of the sub-consultant as well). If a partnership is formed, the Consultants must explain in their EOI submission (a) the justification for forming the partnership and (b) the proposed role and qualifications of each Joint Venture member and/or sub-consultant in executing the assignment. Failure to provide this explanation in the EOI may result in the disqualification of the partnership from the shortlist. Please note that in the evaluation of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of Joint Venture members will be considered, while the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be taken into account.
  5. The selection criteria are as follows, with special emphasis on the Consultant’s specific experience related to the assignment:
  1. The Consultant (as a firm) must have at least 10 years of general experience in providing construction supervision services prior to the deadline for proposal submission. Experience in providing such services in Türkiye will be considered an asset.
  2. The Consultant (as a firm) must have specific experience in providing similar consulting services under contracts of comparable size, type, and complexity within the last ten years prior to the proposal submission deadline.

Note: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting/selection criteria, Consultants must submit at least the following supporting documents. A consulting firm can only use its own qualifications and experience, not those of its parent, sister, or subsidiary companies or its employees.
(i) Company registration/trade/license certificates issued by the relevant government authority in the country of establishment.
(ii) Company brochures indicating the firm's core business areas.
(iii) Completed Form (Annex: Form 1) providing information on similar contracts. This information should include the contract name and reference number, a brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, contract duration, the name of the client and the country in which the assignment was carried out, and the role of the Consultant in the contract. Copies of completion certificates or client references are not required at the EOI stage. However, at a later stage, during the proposal submission phase, the Client may request shortlisted consultants to submit such completion certificates.

(It is kindly requested from the interested firms to provide the information above with an excel sheet given in the below.)

 

Interested Consultants are directed to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing (Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services) (Fourth Edition, November 2020), which outline the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.bid_description: Recrutement d'une firme pour la surveillance et contrôle des travaux de l'extension de la dorsale de la fibre optique
procnotices.notice_text:
PROJET DE TRANSFORMATION NUMERIQUE « PTN »

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 ASSISTANCE TECHNIQUE POUR LE SUIVI ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTION DU RESEAU BACKBONE EN FIBRE OPTIQUE DE LA DORSALE NATIONALE (11600 Km)

 

P180496

N° Avis : AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS

N° de l’Accord du financement Crédit IDA : 7602-ZR

N° de la Convention de Crédit AFD      : CCD119801 H

N° de référence du marché PPM : ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS

 

Date : Le 23 septembre 2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 400 millions de dollars américains pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Transformation Numérique de la RDC(PTN) et cofinancé par l'Agence Française de Développement à la hauteur de 100 millions d’euros.

Le projet est géré par une Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) qui a été mise en place au sein du Ministère des Postes, Télécommunications (MPT) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de Consultant firme chargé de l’Assistance Technique pour le suivi et contrôle des travaux de construction du réseau backbone en fibre optique de la dorsale nationale (11600 km).

L’extension de la dorsale nationale en fibre vise à étendre l’accès aux services haut débit et numériques sur l’ensemble du territoire, à désenclaver numériquement les provinces, à interconnecter la RDC avec les pays voisins et les câbles sous-marins, et à fiabiliser le maillage national de la dorsale optique.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PTN (« UGP PTN »), agissant pour le compte du MPT, assure la maîtrise d’ouvrage de cette activité et la gestion des accords conclus avec les Bailleurs.

La construction et l’exploitation du réseau sont organisées selon un modèle de concession (Partenariat Public-Privé) avec financement d’appoint (gap d’investissements) pour une durée de vingt (20) ans. Le réseau est réparti en quatre (4) lots géographiques distincts qui seront attribués à l’issue d’un appel d’offres international à une étape et deux enveloppes.

L’objectif global de la mission est d’assurer, en toute indépendance et pour le compte du Maître d’Ouvrage, le suivi et le contrôle technique des travaux de construction du réseau de fibres optiques sur les quatre lots, afin de garantir la conformité des ouvrages aux spécifications techniques, aux normes de qualité, aux exigences environnementales et sociales et aux délais, et de fournir au Maître d’Ouvrage l’assurance technique nécessaire à la libération progressive du financement d’appoint. Le Consultant exerce également un rôle de conseil auprès du Maître d’Ouvrage dans la définition des standards des installations et la gestion des risques tout au long de la mise en œuvre du Projet.

La mission couvre les travaux réalisés par les Concessionnaires – directement ou par l’intermédiaire de leurs constructeurs et sous-traitants – depuis les études d’exécution et les réceptions usine jusqu’à la réception définitive des ouvrages, pour les composantes passive et active du réseau.

 

Le démarrage de la mission est prévu au mois de juin 2027 pour une durée de quarante (40) mois.

Les termes de référence complets pour le poste ainsi que l’attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD sont disponibles sur le site de mediacongo.net : www.mediacongo.net, sous l’onglet « Offres d’emploi » et sur le site de l’UG PTN : www.ugptn.cd.

 

L’Unité de Gestion de Projet PTN invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 Les critères d’évaluation de manifestations d’intérêt pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

  • Une expérience confirmée dans le suivi et le contrôle de projets de réseaux à fibres optiques ;
  • La maîtrise des normes et techniques de pose, de raccordement et de mesure (passif) et des équipements de transmission et de supervision (actif) ;
  • Une expérience en gestion de projets d’infrastructures de télécommunications et en réglementation/conformité du secteur ;
  • Une expérience pertinente en Afrique, dont au minimum deux (2) missions similaires en nature, envergure ou complexité, justifiées par des Attestations de Bonne Exécution (ou équivalent) au cours des cinq (5) dernières années ;
  • Une expérience documentée de la gestion des aspects environnementaux et sociaux selon les standards de la Banque mondiale (NES), y compris VBG/EAS/HS et PAR (NES 5) ;
  • Une bonne maîtrise des outils de mesure et logiciels de suivi (dont SIG) ;
  • De solides capacités d’analyse, de reporting et de coordination multi-lots ;
  • La maîtrise de la langue française.
  • Une bonne connaissance des normes ISO \ UIT-T dans le domaine des télécommunications et réseaux à fibres optiques.
  • Une expérience de projets financés par la Banque mondiale, l’AFD ou d’autres institutions financières internationales, ainsi qu’une connaissance du contexte de la République Démocratique du Congo, constitueront des atouts.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à cette étape.

 

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, Septième Edition, Septembre 25 (Règlement de passation des marchés), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. Le candidat devra compléter l’Attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD et la retourner dûment signée accompagnée de sa manifestation d’intérêts.

 

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

 

Un Consultant(firme) sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) par mise en concurrence ouverte internationale telle que décrite dans le Règlement de passation des marchés susmentionné.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse physique ci-dessous ou à l’adresse électronique recrutement@ugpatn.cd chaque jour ouvrable de 9 heures à 16 heures locales.

 

L’UG PTN se réserve le droit de vérifier l’authenticité des informations fournies par les candidats aux fins de la présente sélection. Les candidats ayant fourni des informations tronquées ne seront pas retenus pour la suite du processus de passation des marchés.

Les Manifestations d’Intérêt, écrites en langue française, doivent être déposées physiquement à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou Pdf copiable sur une clé USB ou de préférence, envoyées par courrier électronique en format Pdf copiable à l’adresse mail : recrutement@ugpatn.cd au plus tard le 14 octobre 2026 à 14h00’ heures locales (TU+1) et porter clairement la mention :« AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS :Recrutement d’un Consultant firme chargé de  l’Assistance Technique l’Assistance Technique  pour le suivi et contrôle des travaux de construction du réseau backbone en fibre optique de la dorsale nationale (11600 km)»..

 

 

Noel Jean David LITANGA SANGU PAMBA

 

 

                Coordonnateur

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Individual Selection)

Country: Republic of South Sudan

Project: South Sudan Energy Sector Access and Institutional Strengthening Project (ASSIST)

Grant No.: E166-SS

Assignment Title: Legal Expert

Reference No.: SS-MOED-567735-CS-INDV

The Government of South Sudan (GoSS) has received funding from the World Bank towards the cost of implementing Access and Institutional Strengthening Project (ASSIST) and is being implemented by the Ministry of Energy and Dams (MoED) and South Sudan Electricity Corporation (SSEC). The Project seeks to increase access to electricity services and strengthen the institutional capacity of the electricity sector in Juba, Yei, and Upper Nile Region and Bahra-Gazal, in South Sudan. The effective implementation of the Project requires a sound and enabling legal, regulatory, institutional, and contractual framework to support the development and sustainability of electricity infrastructure and services.

MoED intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services (“the Services”) which include procurement of a Legal Expert (Individual Consultant) assignment for a period of Twelve (12) months. The objective of the assignment is to provide independent legal and contractual advisory services to the Project Implementation Unit (PIU), working in close collaboration with the PIU’s technical, legal, transaction, financial, procurement, and other specialist advisors, to ensure that project implementation is legally compliant, contractually robust, commercially appropriate, and aligned with the Financing Agreement, applicable World Bank requirements, and the laws of the Republic of South Sudan.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below;

The Project Manager

South Sudan Energy Sector Access and Institutional Strengthening Project (ASSIST)

Ministry of Energy & Dams

Ministries Complex

Email: assist.projectmoed@gmail.com/ angellabamuleseyo@yahoo.com/ cosmas.loboso@yahoo.com      

MoED now invites eligible individual consultants to apply for the consulting assignment. Interested individual consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services as required in TOR. The submissions should include a cover letter summarizing the relevant experience and indicating its relevance to the assignment at hand.

The expressions of interest should be accompanied with a CV, phone contact, postal and email addresses, copies of relevant academic documents/ qualifications, copies of the appointment letter (s) and evidence of experience, Contract (s) reference(s), or completion certificate(s) of the current or most recent employment.

The individual consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open International Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations. The consultant will be selected based on the following criteria: 

a. Advanced (Masters) degree in Law (LL.B, LL.M, or equivalent) from a recognized university. Additional relevant postgraduate qualifications shall be an added advantage;

b. Be duly qualified and licensed/admitted to practice law in at least one recognized jurisdiction and be eligible to practice or provide legal services in the Republic of South Sudan, including through any applicable authorization, special admission, collaboration with locally admitted counsel, or other arrangements permitted under the laws of South Sudan;

c. Minimum of 10 years of relevant professional experience in:

  • Contract management and administration;
  • Infrastructure, energy, or public sector projects; and
  • Donor-funded projects, including World Bank, AfDB, or similar development partner-funded assignments;

d. Demonstrated experience in:

  • FIDIC or similar contract frameworks;
  • Public procurement and contract implementation;
  • Drafting, reviewing, and negotiating legal, contractual, and regulatory documentation; and
  • Preparation of legal opinions, contractual correspondence, and advisory memoranda;

e. Experience in:

  • Claims management, dispute avoidance, and dispute resolution;
  • Contractual risk assessment and mitigation; and
  • Management of contractual compliance and implementation issues;

f. Strong understanding of:

  • World Bank procurement regulations and contract management frameworks;
  • Fiduciary, governance, and compliance requirements applicable to donor-funded projects; and
  • International best practices in infrastructure and energy sector contracting;

g. Demonstrated experience in international legal practice, including regulatory frameworks, or cross-border advisory assignments, shall be an added advantage; and

h. Excellent legal drafting, analytical, communication, stakeholder engagement, and report-writing skills.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to section III, para 3.14,3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Projects Financing Goods, Works, Non -Consulting and Consulting Services, July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023 and February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

All inquiries should be sent to the following email address:  assist.projectmoed@gmail.com and Copy: angellabamuleseyo@yahoo.com, cosmas.loboso@yahoo.com  

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below in person or by e-mail by 5:00 noon (Local time) October 15,  2026. Submissions should reference “.: SS-MOED-567735-CS-INDV – Legal Expert (Individual Consultant)” in the address/email subject line.

Under Secretary

Ministry of Energy and Dams (MoED),

Access and Institutional Strengthening Project (ASSIST)

Project Implementation Unit (PIU),

procnotices.notice_text:
THE REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT OF ZANZIBAR

MINISTRY OF BLUE ECONONMY AND FISHERIES

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

Country: United Republic of Tanzania.

Name of project: Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project (p.179969).

Assignment title: Consultancy Services for Conduct full Socio-Economic Impact Assessments in Existing and New MCA’s.

REF. NO.: TZ-MBEF-561671-CS-CDS

This request for expression of interests follows the General Procurement Notice for the Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project which appeared in the UN Development Business Online on 5th June 2025.

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar through the United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Tanzania Scaling up Sustainable Marine Fisheries and Aquaculture Management (TASFAM) Project and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing to cover eligible payments under the contract for Consultancy Services for Conduct full Socio-Economic Impact Assessments in Existing and New MCA’s.

The objective of the assignment is to evaluate the legal and socio-economic context of the MPA/MCA including natural resource and land-use rights, community access patterns, and any historical or legacy issues, to establish a comprehensive household-level socio-economic baseline of affected communities and assess the anticipated positive and negative impacts of access restrictions on livelihoods, income, food and nutrition security.

 

The consultant shall be required to carry out the following activities: -

  • Conduct a comprehensive socio-economic assessment of communities affected by or dependent on the MPA/MCA.
  • Assess the potential socio-economic impacts of existing and proposed access restrictions.
  • Assess the legal, institutional and governance arrangements governing natural resource use, fisheries and community access.
  • Develop an appropriate monitoring and evaluation framework with measurable indicators for tracking implementation and outcomes.

Detailed information on the scope can be obtained in the terms of references (TOR) available to the following website:  https://tasfam.blueeconomysmz.go.tz.

The Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries Zanzibar now invites eligible consulting firms to submit their expression of interests in providing these services.  Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience and key experts to perform the services. The qualification and shortlisting criteria shall include: -

  • The firm shall demonstrate a portfolio of at least 5 assignments in the preparation of RAPs, ARAPs, TRPs, or equivalent social safeguards instruments for World Bank-financed or equivalent projects in Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience in the fisheries, coastal, or blue economy sector is an advantage.
  • The firm shall have demonstrated experience of working with communities dependent on natural resources, particularly in contexts involving temporary or permanent displacement.
  • Qualified team of personnel. The firm should indicate list and qualifications of key personnel proposed for this assignment (Cvs are optional).

Attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III paragraph 3.11,3.12 and 3.13 of the World Bank’s procurement regulations for IPF Borrowers Sixth Edition February 2025.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the consultant Guidelines.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08:00 to 15:30 hours local time, from Mondays to Fridays inclusive, except on public holidays.

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by email or by mail,) by Thursday 15th October 2026 on or before 14: 00 hrs local time and addressed to Principal secretary, Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries, Maisara, Zanzibar, P.O. Box 149, Zanzibar and clearly marked “Consultancy Services for Conduct full Socio-Economic Impact Assessments in Existing and New MCA’s."

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Georgia

KAKHETI CONNECTIVITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT 

Project ID: P173782

Loan No: 9361-GE

Assignment Title: International Tunnel Engineer

Reference No. KCIP/CS/ICS-05R

 

The Government of Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Kakheti Connectivity Improvement Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the following services: International Tunnel Engineer. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The CVs of the candidates should cover the requested information.

The International Tunnel Engineer will support the RD in ensuring that all tunnel and tunnel-related components of ongoing and planned road projects are designed, constructed, and maintained in full compliance with relevant Georgian laws, technical regulations, and engineering standards.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following link:

https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/3le1lqwf9mqkvec4q1lei/TOR-of-Tunnel-Engineer.pdf?rlkey=affs3qoy69ipfrxrr7fycxnno&dl=0

The Qualification Requirements for selection of the Consultant are as follows:

  • Master’s Degree or equivalent in Civil Engineering preferably with specialization in tunnel engineering with 8 years of experience in the road sector on a similar position;
  • Minimum of 5 years of International experience in road tunnel design/construction and/or construction supervision assignments on a similar position;
  • Proven experience in preparing detailed design documentation and/or Design Review assignment for highways and related infrastructure including tunnels;
  • Familiarity with national and international Tunnel design standards (e.g., AASHTO, Eurocode; DIN);
  • Ability to utilize and share knowledge and best international practices to benefit works contractors and supervisions consultants.
  • Ability to work both independently and within teams.
  • Possess superior verbal and writing communication skills in English language.

The period of the consultancy services shall be 24 months (with possibility of downstream extension, subject to satisfactory performance) and the remuneration will be time-based.

Note: The Road Department reserves it’s right to verify submitted references and use obtained information for evaluation purposes.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”,  Seventh Edition,  September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: The consultant shall not receive any payment in connection with the assignment except as provided in the contract. The consultant and its affiliates shall not engage in consulting or other activities that conflict with the interest of the Client under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address: info@georoad.ge.

 

Expressions of Interest accompanied by CVs and other relevant information electronically or in printed materials must be delivered to the address below not later than October 30, 2026, 18:00 hours.

The Roads Department of the Ministry of Regional Development and Infrastructure of Georgia (RDMRDI).

procnotices.notice_text:
State Department for Agriculture

Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

               

                         NAIROBI

 

 

                                                                                                            

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES-INDIVIDUAL SELECTION)

 

Country:                     Kenya

Name of project:       Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP)

Project No:                 P177816

Credit No.:                 7328-KE, 7327-KE

 

Assignment Title:      Prioritization of high-impact, transformative investments to sustainably boost  agricultural productivity and commercialization in Kenya's northern and arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL) counties - Individual selection

Reference No.          KE-MOALF-569681-CS-INDV

                                                                                                               

  1. The Government of Kenya has received a Credit from World Bank towards the cost of the Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Prioritization of high-impact, transformative investments to sustainably boost agricultural productivity and commercialization in Kenya's northern and arid and semi-arid lands (ASAL) counties.
  2. The consulting services (“Services”) main objective of the assignment is to identify, rigorously assess, and prioritize a pipeline of transformative agricultural investments capable of sustainably increasing agricultural productivity and commercialization in the target counties while maximizing economic returns, climate resilience, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and investment readiness for public, private, and development partner financing.
  3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignments can be found in the following website: www.kilimo.go.ke
  4. The Services Contracts are expected to be for a period of One Eighty (180 days).
  5. The State Department for Agriculture (the “Client”) through the Food Systems Resilience Project now invites eligible individual (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Interested individuals MUST provide information indicating that they are qualified to perform the services (attach curriculum vitae (CV), copies of documentary evidence of academic qualifications, professional qualifications. The shortlisting criteria are;
    • A Master's degree in Agricultural Economics, Development Economics, Agricultural Development, International Development, Rural Development, or another closely related discipline.
    • A minimum of 10 years’ general experience of progressively responsible professional experience in agricultural transformation, investment planning, food systems development, climate-resilient agriculture, or rural development is required.
    • At least 3 years’ specific experience in designing, evaluating, and prioritizing large-scale agricultural investment programmes, particularly within Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs) or comparable dryland environments and successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar scope and complexity within the last ten (10) years. Experience on assignments financed by the World Bank, other Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs), bilateral development partners, or national governments will be an added advantage.
    • Demonstrated experience working with national governments, county governments, regional organizations, development partners, and private sector stakeholders.                                            iTechnical Competencies

The Individual Consultant shall demonstrate proven expertise in:

  • Agricultural economics, agricultural transformation, and strategic investment planning.
  • Economic and financial appraisal of investments, including cost-benefit analysis, Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), and Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR).
  • Investment prioritization using evidence-based analytical approaches, including Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA).
  • Climate-smart agriculture, sustainable agricultural development, and resilience-building in Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs).
  • Preparation of investment strategies and implementation roadmaps to support public investment planning and resource mobilization.
  • Stakeholder engagement and facilitation, including consultations with national and county governments, the private sector, development partners, and farming communities.
  • Preparation of high-quality analytical reports, policy briefs, and strategic recommendations to support government decision-making.         ii.Leadership and Coordination Capacity

The Individual Consultant shall demonstrate the ability to:

  • Lead complex multidisciplinary assignments involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Coordinate technical inputs from Government ministries, county governments, development partners, research institutions, and private sector actors.
  • Facilitate high-level policy dialogue, stakeholder consultations, and validation workshops.
  • Produce high-quality analytical reports, investment prospectuses, policy briefs, presentations, GIS products, and other decision-support materials suitable for senior government officials and development partners.      6.The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” First Published July 2016 and revised 4th Edition November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.                                            7.An Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.                                                                                       8.Further information can be obtained from FSRP Procurement Offices during official working hours from 0900 to 1700 hours East African Time (EAT) from Monday to Friday excluding lunch hour (1300 to 1400hours EAT) and public holidays.                                                          9.Expressions of interest MUST be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 6th October, 2026 at 1100 hours EAT and be deposited in the tender box clearly marked State Department for Agriculture located at Kilimo house main reception Ground floor, Cathedral Road Nairobi, or send by email to: info@fsrp.go.ke and quote the Assignment title and Contract No. KE-MOALF-569681-CS-INDV in the subject row

 

Address:

The Principal Secretary

State Department for Agriculture

Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

Nairobi, Kenya.

Head Supply Chain Management

For: Principal Secretary

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Development of High-Quality Food Standards, Enhancement of High-Quality Food, and Model Demonstration Sub-Project

For

High-Quality Food Standard System Construction and Promotion Project

Country: People's Republic of China

Name of Project: China Food Safety Improvement Project

Loan No.: IBRD-92130

Assignment Title: High-Quality Food Standard System Construction and Promotion Project (Development of High-Quality Food Standards, Enhancement of High-Quality Food, and Model Demonstration Sub-Project)

Reference No.:  GD-FSS-GAMR-CS09

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services aims to strengthen the research and development of high-quality food standards, carry out publicity and promotion activities, and create demonstration and model enterprises. For detailed scope, deliverables, duration, and other specific requirements, please refer to the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Consultant's competence and strength;
  2. Management and quality control expertise;
  3. Technical capabilities;
  4. Historical experience and performaces.

Note: 

  1. The submitted EOI shall be stamped with the official seal of the consultant.
  2. Key Experts will be not evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank's  "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" (September 2025 version), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the QCBS method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours. Office hours are from 09:00 to 17:00 on working days from September 23 to October 14, 2026

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to Tender Agency (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by 09:00 on October 15, 2026.

 

Tender Agency: China International Tendering Co., Ltd.

Attn: Zhang Zhi, Guo Hujun

Title: Project Managers

Tel.: +86 10-81168424; 010-81168460

E-mail: zhangzhi5@cgci.gt.cn; guohujun@gt.cn

Address: Rm. 2003B, South Tower, Bld. Jinbintengyue, Huaxia Rd. 49-1,, Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, China

Postal Code: 51000

 

Employer: Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation

Attn: Wang Yifei, Chen Lin

Title: First-level Principal Staff Member; Special Cadre, World Bank Loan Project Office

Tel.: 020-38835493; 020-38835248

 

Annex: detailed Terms of Reference (ToR)

Terms of Reference

Project on the Construction, Publicity and Promotion of the High-Quality Food Standard System Implemented by Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation

Package  I: Development of High-Quality Food Standards, High-Quality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative

In order to ensure the effective implementation of Package I (Development of High-Quality Food Standards, High-Quality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative) under the abovementioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Demonstration Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation is responsible for project management, procurement management, contract administration, project acceptance, fund reimbursement and payment, as well as reviewing standard development plans and publicity-promotion activity plans, organizing standard reviews, and strictly ensuring project quality.

A total of USD 10 million of World Bank loan is planned for application. Of this amount, Package I (Development of HighQuality Food Standards, HighQuality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative) under the abovementioned project plans to apply for a World Bank loan of USD 1 million (equivalent to RMB 6.9 million). The engagement of a thirdparty institution serves the following purposes: first, accelerate the development of high-quality food standards, with no fewer than 30 standards completed within two years; second, carry out the highquality food improvement and model demonstration initiatives, including organizing large-scale high-quality food publicity-promotion events (no fewer than six events within two years) and developing model demonstration enterprises for high-quality food (no fewer than six enterprises within two years), and conducting fund management in compliance with relevant requirements.

Expected outcomes of this project include further advancing the development of high-quality food standards in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), and improving the GBA high-quality food standard system. Through advertising, publicity- promotion activities, and the development of model demonstration enterprises for highquality food, stories of highquality food will be well communicated to continuously raise brand recognition and influence, so that highquality food gains wide public acceptance.

The project addresses existing challenges including difficulties in aligning foodrelated rules across the GBA, insufficient coverage in the development of highquality food standards, and inadequate publicitypromotion measures which undermine effective implementation of those standard. Through this project, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation will further enhance the core value of high-quality food brands, develop model demonstration enterprises, organize brand-promotion events, advance highquality development of the GBA, facilitate the popularization and application of highquality food standards (namely the GBA Food Standards), expand brand influence, and support the building of a highquality living circle in the Greater Bay Area.

2. Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of advancing development of high-quality food standards and high-quality food improvement and model demonstration initiative, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel under market regulation. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as “proportion of earlywarnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". The core objectives are specified as follows: 

First, expand coverage of high-quality food standards. Building on the 87 high-quality food standards issued up to 2025, further efforts will be intensified to develop highquality food standards,expand coverage of standards, continuously enrich and improve the high-quality food standard system, and meet the demand for highquality and safe food among residents in Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao.

Second, promote the implementation and application of high-quality food standards. Through highquality food advertising and publicitypromotion activities, as well as highpriority food improvement and model demonstration initiative, enterprises shall be encouraged to formally adopt and apply highquality food standards The project facilitates the extensive circulation of highquality food across online and offline sales channels, and continuously raises the visibility and influence of highquality food..

3. Scope of Services

Total investment for this project amounts to  RMB 6.9 million.

3.1 Scope of Service Recipients

Service recipients cover the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation, as well as provincial, municipal and district/countylevel market regulation authorities. Target users include the general public and six highquality food manufacturing enterprises, among others.

3.2 Service Content

3.2.1 Engage a thirdparty institution to accelerate the development of high-quality food standards, with no fewer than 30 standards completed within two years. The development of highquality food standards shall comply with relevant documents including the Measures for the Administration of HighQuality Food Standards in the GuangdongHong KongMacao Greater Bay Area, the Specification for the Development of HighQuality Food Standards in the GuangdongHong KongMacao Greater Bay Area (Trial), and the Specification for the Development of GBA Standards for Precooked Dishes. 

Annual plans for the development  of high-quality food standard shall be formulated with the following requirements. Firstly, conduct a comprehensive review on the coverage of issued highquality food standards, identify uncovered areas or weak standardsetting links, and give priority to filling standard gaps for key products and critical links. Secondly, conduct in-depth research on the latest laws, regulations and food standards requirements of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao, and give priority to developing the standards for products with distinctive GBA dietary characteristics and large consumption volume. Thirdly, adopt multi-stakeholder participation. Opinions and suggestions from authorities including market regulation, health, and customs shall be fully taken into account.

The standard-development workflow consists of project initiation application, field research, experimental verification, public consultation, review and issuance, Relevant institutions, universities, industry associations and enterprises from Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao shall participate throughout the process.

3.2.2 .Implement highquality food improvement and model demonstration initiative, including organizing largescale publicity and promotion events for highquality food (no less than six events within two years, with a total attendance of no fewer than 2,000 participants), and developing model demonstration enterprises for highquality food (no less than six enterprises within two years; each enterprise shall have at least two products meeting highquality food standard requirements and prominently display the “GBA Standards” logo on product outer packaging).Model demonstration enterprises shall be large-scale food manufacturers within the GBA that voluntarily adopt the "GBA Standards”, with at least two compliant products. The project contractor shall submit a proposed list of demonstration enterprises for review. The development of demonstration enterprises may only proceed after the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation confirms compliance with basic eligibility criteria  See Appendix 1 for further details.

3.3 Service Period

The service period shall commence on the date of contract signing and end on the project closure date (March 31, 2029).

4 Deliverables, Review and Acceptance

4.1 Deliverables

The deliverables required under this project are set out below:

Service Content

Deliverables

Submission Timing / Stage

Development of High-Quality Food Standards (cumulative ≥30 standards in two years)

1.Annual standard development plan

2.Lead organization information and standard  introduction

3.Chinese version of standard text

4.English version of standard text

5.Standard Compilation Explanatory Notes

6. Supporting documents for the standard development process

7.Statement on the application of High-quality food standard

8.Standard issuance announcement

Annual development plan shall be submitted within 1 month after contract signing; further submissions shall be made by December 31, 2027 and December 31, 2028 respectively

High-Quality Food Publicity and Promotion

1.Annual publicity and promotion  plan

2.One promotional video for highquality food standards (duration: 510 minutes)

3.Batch of promotional materials (≥1,500 brochures, ≥70 roll-up banners, ≥70 leaflet designs)

4.Supporting documents for targeted distribution of promotional materials

5.Supporting documents verifying ≥6 promotion events with total attendance ≥2,000

Annual publicity and promotion plan shall be submitted within 1 month after contract signing; further submissions shall be made by December 31, 2027 and December 31, 2028 respectively

Development of High-Quality Food Model Demonstration Enterprises (cumulative ≥6 enterprises in two years)
